name: Pete Hunt
milestone_by_age_26: As an early React team member at Facebook/Instagram, helped take React from an internal experimental UI library to a public open-source release (JSConf US, May 2013) and became its primary external evangelist through conference talks that reversed initial community hostility.
early_history_summary: Grew up coding from about age nine on a monochrome home computer; attended Cornell University (BA Information Science, MS Computer Science via a 4+1 program), graduating around 2010–2011. After a weak first career-fair cycle, he spent a year grinding algorithm interviews, then joined Facebook in 2011 at about age 22; he later moved to Instagram post-acquisition and bet the Instagram web app on Jordan Walke's experimental React.
family_context_summary: Grew up in a small town in the northeastern United States; parents brought home an early computer and encouraged science/technical interests. Family financial status not documented in detail.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as domain-expert parents; they supplied an early home computer and general science encouragement rather than software industry apprenticeship.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Facebook/Instagram, React internal platform, Cornell, conference circuit
evidence_summary: Hunt learned to program as a child, studied at Cornell, and joined Facebook in 2011 at ~22. After Instagram's acquisition he became the first Facebook engineer embedded full-time, chose React for Instagram Web, and drove open-sourcing and external adoption in 2013 at about age 24. Family background shows early computer access but not elite domain inheritance; the decisive stack was Facebook's product surface, engineering culture, and the mobile/web UI structural wave.
starting_point: Raised in a small northeastern U.S. town; parents encouraged science and supplied an early home computer; middle-class technical-curious household otherwise not fully documented.
current_position: Software engineering leader and former CEO of Dagster Labs / Elementl (Dagster open-source data orchestration); previously CEO of Smyte (acquired by Twitter) and React pioneer at Facebook/Instagram.

trajectory.event: Joined Facebook as a software engineer out of Cornell graduate school after a 7-for-7 full-time interview cycle.
Helped open-source React and became its lead external evangelist after betting Instagram Web on the experimental library.
Co-founded Smyte, an anti-abuse/trust-and-safety startup applying lessons from Instagram/Facebook safety systems.
Smyte launched publicly and went through Y Combinator with seed and Series A funding.
Smyte was acquired by Twitter; Hunt continued in trust-and-safety and data engineering roles.
Joined Elementl (Dagster) as head of engineering and later became CEO of the data orchestration company.

early_history_summary: Auslander earned a BA in mathematics from Princeton University in 1963 and spent his career at IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, contributing to the PL.8 compiler and RISC systems. He was named IBM Fellow in 1991 and elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 1996.
evidence_summary: Long IBM Research career with major mid-career honors for RISC/compiler work. No independently dated material breakout at or before age 26 was identified; birth year is missing from public bios.

name: Sheryl Sandberg
milestone_by_age_26: No material career-defining milestone by age 26 for this project's bar. By 26 she held elite credentials (Harvard AB summa/Phi Beta Kappa 1991; HBS MBA highest distinction 1995; brief McKinsey stint) but her distinctive professional breakouts—Google online sales/ops leadership (from 2001, age ~32) and Facebook/Meta COO (2008, age 38)—came later.
early_history_summary: Born August 28, 1969 in Washington, D.C.; raised in North Miami Beach, Florida. Harvard economics summa cum laude (1991), World Bank research assistant to Lawrence Summers, Harvard Business School MBA (1995), McKinsey (~1995–96), then Treasury chief of staff to Summers (1996–2001). Joined Google in 2001 and Facebook as COO in 2008.
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family; father Joel Sandberg an ophthalmologist; mother Adele a college French professor. Professional middle/upper-middle class household in South Florida.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were medical and academic professionals, not technology-industry operators; domain transfer to tech operating leadership is not direct.
evidence_summary: Sandberg’s path through Harvard, Summers mentorship, and McKinsey/Treasury is well documented, but the milestones that made her a global technology figure (Google ad sales scale-up; Facebook COO) occurred well after age 26. Elite education alone is not coded as the required material ≤26 milestone here.

name: Larry Kaplan
milestone_by_age_26: No verified material milestone at age ≤26. Studied UC Berkeley 1968–1974 (CS), joined Atari August 1976 and programmed 2600 launch titles Combat, Air-Sea Battle, and Street Racer (1977), later co-founding Activision (1979) and creating Kaboom! (1981). Approximate birth ~1950 implies 1977 launch titles at ~27 and Activision at ~29; exact birth year missing, so age ≤26 cannot be confirmed.
early_history_summary: Berkeley CS graduate (1974) who worked at Control Systems Industries before joining Atari as an early VCS programmer, then left with peers to help found Activision. Later worked at Amiga-related ventures, Capcom, 3DO, and briefly as technical director on Antz at PDI.
evidence_summary: Important early home-console programmer, but without a confirmed birth year the Atari 2600 launch work and Activision founding cannot be locked to age ≤26; available college dates point to milestones around age 27+.

name: Ivan Zhang
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Cohere in 2019 with Aidan Gomez and Nick Frosst—a material founding event—but birth year is not documented in reviewed sources, so age at founding cannot be independently verified as ≤26 (he is a U of T contemporary of Gomez b. ~1996–97 and founder of FOR.ai, but age is unconfirmed).
early_history_summary: Born in Shenzhen, China; moved to Toronto at age eight. Built digital stamina through gaming, then university hackathons; founded FOR.ai research group and co-founded Cohere in Toronto in 2019, focusing on enterprise LLMs.
family_context_summary: Immigrant family from Shenzhen to Toronto; parents worked hard in menial labor jobs so children could be educated—cited by Zhang as motivation. Financial details otherwise not quantified.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented as tech-domain experts; immigrant work ethic rather than industry apprenticeship.
evidence_summary: Cohere co-founding is a major achievement and he appears young relative to peers, but without a confirmed birth year the project rules require marking age_26_ineligible rather than assuming age ≤26.
